dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Magnetics maps the architecture. Electrical methods go after the ore minerals themselves.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Push a current into the ground between two electrodes, measure the voltage between two others, and you get resistivity — how hard the ground is to push current through.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: A fault zone full of clay and water is conductive. A silicified, quartz-flooded vein is resistive. In gold systems the resistive high is often the vein itself.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Then the better trick. Cut the current, and watch the voltage.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: It does not drop to zero. It decays — because the ground stored charge. That is induced polarisation. And what stores charge best is disseminated metallic sulphides: pyrite, arsenopyrite, chalcopyrite.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Gold itself is invisible to every geophysical method ever built. There is far too little of it. But the sulphides it precipitated with are not invisible, and chargeability maps those directly.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Geometry decides what you can see. Electrodes are laid out in an array, and the rule is blunt: depth of investigation is roughly a fifth to a third of the array length.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Want to see two hundred metres down? Lay out a kilometre.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: The raw result is a pseudo-section — measurements plotted at a made-up depth. It is not a picture of the ground, and reading it as one is the classic beginner mistake.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Inversion fixes that. A computer builds a model of the subsurface, predicts what the survey would have read, compares it with what was actually read, and adjusts until the two agree.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: Out comes a model you can draw a drillhole on. But many different models fit the same data, so you constrain it with geology — and never trust a feature at the very bottom edge.

dialogue.speaker: juma
dialogue.text: So which survey do you believe?

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: The one that agrees with the others.

dialogue.speaker: zawadi
dialogue.text: A magnetic low on an altered shear. A resistivity high where it is silicified. A chargeability high where the sulphides sit. Arsenic in the soil above it. One of those is a maybe. All four is a drill target.
